original_question: Among compact surfaces immersed in Euclidean 3-space E^3, are the ordinary spheres the only compact surfaces whose immersion is of finite type, meaning that the position vector splits into finitely many Laplace eigensections?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Conjecture 1: The only compact surfaces of finite type in E^3 are the ordinary spheres. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient space E^3, the compactness hypothesis, the finite-type condition as a finite Laplace-spectral decomposition of the position vector, and the intended conclusion that only ordinary spheres should occur. This matches Section 3, Conjecture 1, rather than the broader classification Problem 1 or the broader related Conjectures 1.A and 1.B. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
missing_details: The paper defines finite type for an isometric immersion x:M→E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold M, so a fully stand-alone version should specify that the surface carries the induced metric and that Δ is the Laplace operator on M. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

The finite-type condition should be written explicitly as x=c+x1+...+xk, where c is a constant vector in E^3 and x1,...,xk are nonconstant E^3-valued maps satisfying Δxi=λi xi. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

The eigenvalues λ1,...,λk do not need to be distinct for 'finite type'; distinctness is only part of the stronger notion of k-type. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

The paper does not impose embeddedness, orientability, or extra curvature assumptions; the scope is simply compact surfaces immersed in E^3. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

To remove ambiguity, 'ordinary spheres' should be read as ordinary round 2-spheres in E^3. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

For compact M, the nearby context gives an equivalent reformulation via a nontrivial polynomial Q with Q(Δ)(x−c)=0, equivalently Q(Δ)H=0, where H is the mean curvature vector. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))

No extra algebraic data are part of the paper's statement: there is no ambient field or ring choice, no homogeneity or degree restriction, no nilpotency condition, and no 'for all sufficiently large' quantifier in this problem. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
refined_question: Let x:M→E^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact connected surface into Euclidean 3-space, and let Δ be the Laplace operator of the induced metric on M. Suppose x is of finite type, in the sense that its position vector admits a decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk for some constant vector c∈E^3 and finitely many nonconstant E^3-valued maps xi satisfying Δxi=λi xi. Must the immersed surface x(M) be an ordinary round 2-sphere in E^3? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent compact-case formulation: let x:M→E^3 be an isometric immersion of a compact connected surface with mean curvature vector H. If there exist a constant vector c∈E^3 and a nontrivial polynomial Q such that Q(Δ)(x−c)=0, equivalently Q(Δ)H=0, must x(M) be an ordinary round 2-sphere in E^3? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
justification: Section 3 first states the broader Problem 1 of classifying all finite type hypersurfaces in E^{n+1}, and then singles out the compact-surface case in E^3 as Conjecture 1. Your draft clearly targets that narrower compact E^3 conjecture, not the broader all-surfaces problem and not the related but broader Conjectures 1.A and 1.B. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950)) The needed hidden notation comes from Section 2.1, where finite type is defined via the spectral decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk with Δxi=λi xi for an isometric immersion x:M→E^m of a connected Riemannian manifold. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950)) Section 2.2 then provides the only explicit paper-level equivalent reformulation nearby: for compact M, finite type is equivalent to the existence of a constant vector c and a nontrivial polynomial Q with Q(Δ)(x−c)=0, equivalently Q(Δ)H=0. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950)) This is a differential-geometric conjecture, so algebraic items such as ambient field/ring, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers are not part of its content. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/download/1564/1137/3950))
